name: Woolly mammoth
what: Shaggy, small-eared elephants of the mammoth steppe, from Ireland to Alaska.
why: Gone from the mainland about 10,500 years ago; a dwarfed population survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, when the pyramids already stood.

sources.cite: Stuart, A. J., "Late Quaternary megafaunal extinctions on the continents: a short review", Geological Journal 50, 338-363 (2015)
Vartanyan, S. L. et al., "Holocene dwarf mammoths from Wrangel Island in the Siberian Arctic", Nature 362, 337-340 (1993)

name: Woolly rhinoceros
what: A two-horned rhino with a thick coat, grazing the cold steppes of Eurasia.
why: It held on in north-east Siberia until about 14,000 years ago, then vanished in the warm Bølling-Allerød spell.

sources.cite: Stuart, A. J. & Lister, A. M., "Extinction chronology of the woolly rhinoceros Coelodonta antiquitatis in the context of late Quaternary megafaunal extinctions in northern Eurasia", Quaternary Science Reviews 51, 1-17 (2012)
Lord, E. et al., "Pre-extinction demographic stability and genomic signatures of adaptation in the woolly rhinoceros", Current Biology 30, 3871-3879 (2020)

name: Giant deer
what: The "Irish elk": a deer with antlers up to 3.6 m across.
why: Its last herds lived in western Siberia until about 7,700 years ago, long after the mammoths left Europe.

sources.cite: Stuart, A. J. et al., "Pleistocene to Holocene extinction dynamics in giant deer and woolly mammoth", Nature 431, 684-689 (2004)

name: Cave bear
what: A huge, mostly plant-eating bear that hibernated in caves; Neanderthals and modern humans used the same caves.
why: It died out about 24,000 years ago, at the coldest time, perhaps squeezed by people taking its caves.

sources.cite: Pacher, M. & Stuart, A. J., "Extinction chronology and palaeobiology of the cave bear (Ursus spelaeus)", Boreas 38, 189-206 (2009)

name: Sabre-toothed cat
what: A heavy cat with 28 cm canines that ambushed large grazers in the Americas.
why: It vanished with its prey around 12,000 to 10,000 years ago, soon after people spread through the Americas.

sources.cite: Stuart, A. J., "Late Quaternary megafaunal extinctions on the continents: a short review", Geological Journal 50, 338-363 (2015)

name: Giant ground sloth
what: A ground sloth as big as an elephant that could rear up to browse trees.
why: Gone about 12,000 years ago, within a couple of thousand years of people reaching the pampas.

sources.cite: Stuart, A. J., "Late Quaternary megafaunal extinctions on the continents: a short review", Geological Journal 50, 338-363 (2015)

name: Diprotodon
what: The largest marsupial ever: a three-tonne wombat relative that roamed Australia in herds.
why: It disappeared around 45,000 years ago, a few thousand years after people arrived.

sources.cite: Roberts, R. G. et al., "New ages for the last Australian megafauna: continent-wide extinction about 46,000 years ago", Science 292, 1888-1892 (2001)
Wroe, S. et al., "Climate change frames debate over the extinction of megafauna in Sahul", PNAS 110, 8777-8781 (2013)
